gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch is massively over-scoped relative to the stated issue. The issue asks to (1) change schema generation from Workflow to ForgeConfig, (2) update the schema fixture. The gold patch does this but also: removes the entire Workflow type from forge_domain, removes WorkflowService trait, refactors apply_workflow_config to apply_env across multiple crates, moves workflow config fields into Environment, adds new fields to ForgeConfig (tool_supported), removes SummaryTag from Compact, updates CLI to remove workflow flag, and restructures the entire configuration flow across ~20 files. The schema-specific changes (adding JsonSchema derives, updating forge.schema.json) are correct and address the issue.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The base should fail the test because ForgeConfig does not derive JsonSchema, so schemars::schema_for!(ForgeConfig) would not compile. The gold patch adds JsonSchema derives to ForgeConfig and all its sub-types, so the test should pass. However, there is a critical concern: if the test uses the is_ci pattern (like the existing workflow test in forge_domain), CI env var is NOT set in this Docker environment, meaning the test would just write the schema file and always pass (even without the gold patch's changes, as long as ForgeConfig compiles with JsonSchema). The gold patch adds is_ci as a dev-dependency to forge_config, strongly suggesting the test uses this pattern.
too_narrow_risks: Test only validates schema generation for ForgeConfig, not the massive Workflow removal and service refactoring in the gold patch
Only one test (generate_workflow_schema) is run - no compilation check of other modified crates
If the test uses the is_ci pattern and CI is not set in Docker, the test always passes as long as ForgeConfig derives JsonSchema - it doesn't even check forge.schema.json content
A minimal solution (just add JsonSchema derive to ForgeConfig + sub-types, add dev-deps) could pass without updating forge.schema.json or removing Workflow
Test does not verify that several sub-types (RetryConfig, HttpConfig, ModelConfig, AutoDumpFormat, TlsVersion, TlsBackend) correctly derive JsonSchema - only that ForgeConfig as a whole does
No test for the tool_supported field being added to ForgeConfig
too_broad_risks: The gold patch modifies ~20 files across 6 crates but the test only checks one narrow behavior in forge_config
implementation_coupling: If the test compares schema JSON (when CI is set), it requires exact JSON match of the full ForgeConfig schema, meaning any alternative field ordering, description wording, or type representation would fail
The test name generate_workflow_schema is reused from the old test, coupling it to the gold's naming convention
environment_risks: Critical: CI environment variable is not set in the Docker container. If the test uses is_ci::uncached() (as strongly suggested by is_ci being a dev-dependency in the gold patch), the test would always pass by writing the schema file rather than comparing it, making verification meaningless
The test patch file is not available in the audit materials (/tmp/test.patch is absent), so exact test behavior cannot be verified
The test patch must add dev-dependencies (anyhow, is_ci, tokio, serde_json) to Cargo.toml OR the candidate solution must add them - mismatch could cause compilation failure
mismatches: Gold patch scope far exceeds the issue description: issue asks for schema migration, gold removes entire Workflow module and refactors services
Test only covers forge_config package but gold patch modifies forge_domain, forge_app, forge_api, forge_infra, forge_main - these changes are untested
The test is named generate_workflow_schema but is supposed to validate ForgeConfig, not Workflow

evidence.detail: Issue asks to change schema generation to use ForgeConfig instead of Workflow, and update the schema fixture
Gold patch is ~2770 lines, modifying ~20 files across 6 crates, removing Workflow module entirely
Only runs: cargo test --no-fail-fast -p forge_config --test schema generate_workflow_schema (single test in one package)
Base ForgeConfig does NOT derive JsonSchema - test should fail to compile on unmodified base
Base dev-dependencies only has pretty_assertions; gold adds anyhow, is_ci, serde_json, tokio
Existing schema test uses is_ci pattern: CI=compare, local=write. If test patch follows same pattern, CI not being set means test always passes
CI env var is not set in the Docker environment (verified), which affects is_ci::uncached() behavior

summary: The test is too narrow for the gold patch and has a critical environment risk. The gold patch massively over-solves the issue (removes entire Workflow module, refactors services across 6 crates) while the test only checks schema generation in forge_config. More importantly, if the test follows the established is_ci pattern (strongly suggested by is_ci dev-dependency), the CI env var is NOT set in the Docker container, so the test would simply write the schema file and always pass as long as ForgeConfig derives JsonSchema. This means the test may not actually validate schema correctness. The test patch itself is unavailable for direct audit. Recommend: (1) ensure CI=true is set in the eval environment, (2) add compilation tests for other modified crates, or (3) narrow the gold patch to match what the single test actually validates.
